subproblem.title: Closed Euclidean balls have Lebesgue measure at most (2r)^k (printed ω_k r^k, erratum ω_k ≤ 2^k)
subproblem.statement: Let ι be a finite index set with k := |ι| elements and E := ℝ^ι = EuclideanSpace ℝ ι with its Euclidean distance |w − c| = (Σ_{i∈ι}(w_i − c_i)²)^{1/2} and Lebesgue measure L^k (Mathlib's volume on E). For every c ∈ E and every real r ≥ 0, the closed ball B̄_r(c) = {w ∈ E : |w − c| ≤ r} satisfies L^k(B̄_r(c)) ≤ (2r)^k, as an inequality in [0, ∞], i.e. L^k(B̄_r(c)) ≤ ofReal((2r)^k).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (c : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) (r : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → volume (closedBall c r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * r) ^ Fintype.card ι)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof. Simon, Ch. 6, §5, 'Proof of the Deformation Theorem', pp. 163–164, uses the ball volume ω_{n+1}(5σ_ℓ)^{n+1}. By the documented erratum this is replaced by the cube bound (2·5σ_ℓ)^k, since ω_k ≤ 2^k. Here the bound is proved for an arbitrary centre c and an arbitrary radius r ≥ 0.

Notation. For w ∈ E, w_i (i ∈ ι) are its coordinates, so |w − c| = (Σ_{i∈ι}(w_i − c_i)²)^{1/2}. Let ofLp : E → ℝ^ι = (ι → ℝ), w ↦ (w_i)_{i∈ι}, be the coordinate map. On ℝ^ι use the sup-distance d_∞(v, v′) = max_{i∈ι}|v_i − v′_i| (0 if ι = ∅) and the product Lebesgue measure volume = ⊗_{i∈ι} L¹. Write ofReal(t) := max(t, 0).

1. Coordinates are 1-Lipschitz. For w, c ∈ E and i ∈ ι, (w_i − c_i)² ≤ Σ_{j∈ι}(w_j − c_j)², because all summands are ≥ 0. Taking square roots, |w_i − c_i| ≤ |w − c|.
2. Inclusion in a cube. Let Q := {v ∈ ℝ^ι : d_∞(v, ofLp c) ≤ r}; since r ≥ 0, Q = ∏_{i∈ι}[c_i − r, c_i + r]. If w ∈ B̄_r(c), then by step 1 |w_i − c_i| ≤ |w − c| ≤ r for every i ∈ ι. Hence d_∞(ofLp w, ofLp c) ≤ r, i.e. ofLp w ∈ Q. Thus B̄_r(c) ⊆ ofLp⁻¹(Q).
3. Lebesgue measure on E is the product Lebesgue measure in the coordinates. The coordinate map ofLp is a measurable bijection with measurable inverse. It is measure preserving from L^k = volume on E to the product measure on ℝ^ι (Mathlib: PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, equivalently EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp). Q is closed, hence Borel measurable, so L^k(ofLp⁻¹(Q)) = volume(Q).
4. Volume of the cube. By the product formula, volume(Q) = ∏_{i∈ι} L¹([c_i − r, c_i + r]) = ∏_{i∈ι}(2r) = (2r)^k. This equals ofReal((2r)^k) because 2r ≥ 0 (Mathlib: Real.volume_pi_closedBall, which needs r ≥ 0). If k = 0, then E and ℝ^ι are one-point spaces of measure 1 = (2r)^0, and the same chain applies.
5. Conclusion. By monotonicity of the (outer) measure L^k and steps 2–4, L^k(B̄_r(c)) ≤ L^k(ofLp⁻¹(Q)) = volume(Q) = ofReal((2r)^k). ∎
proof_key_steps: Hence B̄_r(c) ⊆ ofLp⁻¹(Q) with Q = ∏_i [c_i − r, c_i + r], the sup-metric closed ball about ofLp c.
ofLp : E → ℝ^ι is measure preserving (Lebesgue measure on E is the product measure) and Q is closed, so L^k(ofLp⁻¹ Q) = volume(Q).
volume(Q) = (2r)^k for r ≥ 0, so L^k(B̄_r(c)) ≤ ofReal((2r)^k) by monotonicity.

audit.reason: The prose and exact one-line type agree, including arbitrary finite ι, arbitrary centre and r ≥ 0. Coordinate domination gives inclusion in the sup-metric cube; the measure-preserving coordinate map and product-volume formula yield the stated ENNReal bound. The proof handles r = 0 and dimension zero, is complete, and uses no child or parent conclusion.

subproblem.title: Periodic lattice tubes about nearby centres with disjoint base balls are disjoint (printed 'pairwise disjoint collection')
subproblem.statement: Let ι be a finite index set and E := ℝ^ι = EuclideanSpace ℝ ι with its Euclidean distance |·|. For g ∈ E and τ ∈ ℝ let U(g, τ) := {y ∈ E : there is z ∈ ℤ^ι with Σ_{i∈ι}(y_i − g_i − z_i)² < τ²}. Let g₀, b, b′ ∈ E and σ, σ′ ∈ ℝ satisfy |b − g₀| < 1/4, |b′ − g₀| < 1/4, 0 < σ < 1/4 and 0 < σ′ < 1/4. Assume the closed balls B̄_σ(b) = {w ∈ E : |w − b| ≤ σ} and B̄_{σ′}(b′) = {w ∈ E : |w − b′| ≤ σ′} are disjoint. Then U(b, σ) and U(b′, σ′) are disjoint.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (g₀ b b' : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) (σ σ' : ℝ), dist b g₀ < 1 / 4 → dist b' g₀ < 1 / 4 → 0 < σ → σ < 1 / 4 → 0 < σ' → σ' < 1 / 4 → Disjoint (closedBall b σ) (closedBall b' σ') → Disjoint {y : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι | ∃ z : ι → ℤ, ∑ i, (y i - b i - z i) ^ 2 < σ ^ 2} {y : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι | ∃ z : ι → ℤ, ∑ i, (y i - b' i - z i) ^ 2 < σ' ^ 2}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof. It proves Simon's parenthetical claim (Ch. 6, §5, p. 164) that 'p_j⁻¹B_{σ_ℓ}(b_ℓ + z), ℓ = 1, 2, …, z ∈ ℤ^{n+ℓ} ∩ S_j, is a pairwise disjoint collection'. Here the claim is proved for the periodic open sets in E, before pulling back by the projection; in the parent, U(b, σ_b) = ⋃_z B_{σ_b}(b + z) and T(b, σ_b) = p⁻¹(U(b, σ_b)).

Notation. For y, g ∈ E and z ∈ ℤ^ι, write g + z and y − z for the points of E with coordinates g_i + z_i and y_i − z_i. Regard z itself as the point of E with coordinates z_i. |v| = (Σ_i v_i²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean norm, and B̄_ρ(c) = {w ∈ E : |w − c| ≤ ρ}.

1. Squared distances. For y, g ∈ E and z ∈ ℤ^ι, the vector y − (g + z) has coordinates y_i − g_i − z_i, so |y − (g + z)|² = Σ_{i∈ι}(y_i − g_i − z_i)². Let τ > 0 with Σ_i(y_i − g_i − z_i)² < τ². Then |y − (g + z)| < τ: otherwise |y − (g + z)| ≥ τ > 0 would give |y − (g + z)|² ≥ τ².
2. Setup. Suppose, for a contradiction, that y ∈ U(b, σ) ∩ U(b′, σ′). Then there are z, z′ ∈ ℤ^ι with Σ_i(y_i − b_i − z_i)² < σ² and Σ_i(y_i − b′_i − z′_i)² < σ′². Since σ > 0 and σ′ > 0, step 1 gives |y − (b + z)| < σ and |y − (b′ + z′)| < σ′.
3. Case z = z′. Put w := y − z. Comparing coordinates (y_i − z_i − b_i = y_i − b_i − z_i), w − b = y − (b + z) and w − b′ = y − (b′ + z). Hence |w − b| < σ and |w − b′| < σ′, so w ∈ B̄_σ(b) ∩ B̄_{σ′}(b′). This contradicts the hypothesis that these closed balls are disjoint.
4. Case z ≠ z′. By the triangle inequality and translation invariance of the distance (|(b + z) − (g₀ + z)| = |b − g₀|):
   |y − (g₀ + z)| ≤ |y − (b + z)| + |b − g₀| < σ + 1/4 < 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2.
   In the same way, |y − (g₀ + z′)| ≤ |y − (b′ + z′)| + |b′ − g₀| < σ′ + 1/4 < 1/2. Hence, again by translation invariance and the triangle inequality:
   |z − z′| = |(g₀ + z) − (g₀ + z′)| ≤ |(g₀ + z) − y| + |y − (g₀ + z′)| < 1/2 + 1/2 = 1.
   On the other hand z ≠ z′, so z_j ≠ z′_j for some j ∈ ι. Then z_j − z′_j is a nonzero integer, so |z_j − z′_j| ≥ 1. Since (z_j − z′_j)² ≤ Σ_i(z_i − z′_i)² = |z − z′|², we get |z − z′| ≥ |z_j − z′_j| ≥ 1. Contradiction.
5. Both cases are impossible, so no point lies in U(b, σ) ∩ U(b′, σ′); that is, U(b, σ) and U(b′, σ′) are disjoint. ∎
proof_key_steps: |y − (g + z)|² = Σ_i (y_i − g_i − z_i)², so for τ > 0 the defining inequality gives |y − (g + z)| < τ.
A common point y yields z, z′ ∈ ℤ^ι with |y − (b + z)| < σ and |y − (b′ + z′)| < σ′.
If z = z′, then w = y − z lies in B̄_σ(b) ∩ B̄_{σ′}(b′), contradicting their disjointness.
If z ≠ z′, then |y − (g₀ + z)|, |y − (g₀ + z′)| < 1/2 give |z − z′| < 1, whereas some |z_j − z′_j| ≥ 1 gives |z − z′| ≥ 1: contradiction.

audit.reason: Every centre, radius and disjointness hypothesis is present in both statements and used correctly. Positive radii convert the squared inequalities into distance bounds. Equal lattice translates contradict base-ball disjointness; unequal translates force lattice distance both below 1 and at least 1. This proves exactly the stated disjointness without circular reliance or a missing dimensional assumption.

- ball_volume: PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, Real.volume_pi_closedBall, PiLp.dist_apply_le and dist_pi_le_iff.
- tubes_disjoint: EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, PiLp.dist_apply_le and Int.one_le_abs.
- vitali_bound: Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall (τ = 5) and measure_biUnion_le. SimonGMT's Chapter01.exists_fiveTimesCovering is an equivalent alternative.
- Parent glue: Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion and tsum_meas_le_meas_iUnion_of_disjoint.

All three child types validate and elaborate in the comparator's exact contract scope. All were fully proved in scratch, and Submission.dgc_periodic_maximal was kernel-checked from them with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] and no sorry. No name collides with anything, and no Matrix/IsUnit construction occurs.

subproblem.title: 5-times covering packing bound: L^k(S) ≤ 10^k M (printed (4) and L^{n+1}(B_j) ≤ β⁻¹5^{n+1}ω_{n+1})
subproblem.statement: Let ι be a finite index set with k := |ι| elements, and E := ℝ^ι = EuclideanSpace ℝ ι with its Euclidean distance and Lebesgue outer measure L^k (Mathlib's volume, evaluated on arbitrary sets). Let S ⊆ E be any set (not assumed measurable), r : E → ℝ, and R, M ∈ ℝ with 0 < r(b) ≤ R for every b ∈ S. Write ofReal(t) := max(t, 0) ∈ [0, ∞). Assume the packing condition: for every u ⊆ S such that the closed balls B̄_{r(b)}(b) = {w : |w − b| ≤ r(b)}, b ∈ u, are pairwise disjoint (distinct b, b′ ∈ u give disjoint balls), u is countable and Σ_{b∈u} ofReal(r(b)^k) ≤ ofReal(M) in [0, ∞]. Then L^k(S) ≤ ofReal(10^k · M).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)) (r : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι → ℝ) (R M : ℝ), (∀ b ∈ S, 0 < r b ∧ r b ≤ R) → (∀ u ⊆ S, u.PairwiseDisjoint (fun b => closedBall b (r b)) → u.Countable ∧ ∑' b : u, ENNReal.ofReal (r b ^ Fintype.card ι) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal M) → volume S ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (10 ^ Fintype.card ι * M)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4, 8 and 9 of the parent proof. Simon, Ch. 6, §5, pp. 163–164, prints (4): 'by the 5-times Covering Lemma 3.4 of Ch. 1 there is a pairwise disjoint subcollection {B_{σ_ℓ}(b_ℓ)} of the collection {B_{σ_b}(b)}_{b∈B_j} such that B_j ⊆ ⋃_ℓ B_{5σ_ℓ}(b_ℓ)'. It then concludes: 'Thus by (4) we conclude L^{n+1}(B_j) ≤ β⁻¹5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}'.
- The summation bound Σ_ℓ σ_ℓ^{n+1} ≤ β⁻¹ (parent steps 5–7) appears here as the packing hypothesis, with M in place of β⁻¹.
- Per the parent's errata, the covering lemma is applied to closed balls.
- The printed ω_k(5σ)^k is bounded by (10σ)^k through the sibling ball_volume (erratum ω_k ≤ 2^k).
Notation: ofReal(t) := max(t, 0) ∈ [0, ∞); B̄_ρ(c) = {w ∈ E : |w − c| ≤ ρ}; all sums are in [0, ∞].

1. Covering (printed (4)). The closed balls B̄_{r(b)}(b), b ∈ S, have radii r(b) ≤ R. Apply the 5-times covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4). In Mathlib this is Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall with index set S, centres x(b) = b, radii r, bound R and enlargement factor τ = 5 > 3. It holds for any family of closed balls with radii bounded above in a (pseudo)metric space. It gives u ⊆ S such that:
   - the balls B̄_{r(b)}(b), b ∈ u, are pairwise disjoint, and
   - for every a ∈ S there is b ∈ u with B̄_{r(a)}(a) ⊆ B̄_{5r(b)}(b).
   Since r(a) > 0, a ∈ B̄_{r(a)}(a). Hence S ⊆ ⋃_{b∈u} B̄_{5r(b)}(b). (If S = ∅, take u = ∅.)
2. Packing. Apply the packing hypothesis to this u, which is legitimate because u ⊆ S and its balls are pairwise disjoint. So u is countable and Σ_{b∈u} ofReal(r(b)^k) ≤ ofReal(M).
3. Volume of the enlarged balls (sibling ball_volume). For b ∈ u, 5r(b) ≥ 0 because r(b) > 0, so L^k(B̄_{5r(b)}(b)) ≤ ofReal((2·5r(b))^k). Moreover (2·5r(b))^k = (10 r(b))^k = 10^k·r(b)^k, and ofReal(s·t) = ofReal(s)·ofReal(t) for s = 10^k ≥ 0. Hence L^k(B̄_{5r(b)}(b)) ≤ ofReal(10^k)·ofReal(r(b)^k).
4. Conclusion (printed L^{n+1}(B_j) ≤ β⁻¹5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}). L^k is an outer measure: it is monotone and countably subadditive on arbitrary sets, so S need not be measurable. Therefore:
   L^k(S) ≤ L^k(⋃_{b∈u} B̄_{5r(b)}(b))          (monotonicity, step 1)
          ≤ Σ_{b∈u} L^k(B̄_{5r(b)}(b))            (countable subadditivity; u is countable by step 2)
          ≤ Σ_{b∈u} ofReal(10^k)·ofReal(r(b)^k)  (step 3)
          = ofReal(10^k)·Σ_{b∈u} ofReal(r(b)^k)  (a constant factor comes out of a sum in [0, ∞])
          ≤ ofReal(10^k)·ofReal(M)               (step 2; multiplication is monotone in [0, ∞])
          = ofReal(10^k·M)                        (since 10^k ≥ 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: 5-times (Vitali) covering with τ = 5 and radii ≤ R gives u ⊆ S with pairwise disjoint balls B̄_{r(b)}(b) and S ⊆ ⋃_{b∈u} B̄_{5r(b)}(b) (printed (4)).
The packing hypothesis for this u gives: u countable and Σ_{b∈u} ofReal(r(b)^k) ≤ ofReal(M).
Sibling ball_volume: L^k(B̄_{5r(b)}(b)) ≤ ofReal((10 r(b))^k) = ofReal(10^k)·ofReal(r(b)^k).
Monotonicity and countable subadditivity of the outer measure give L^k(S) ≤ ofReal(10^k)·Σ_{b∈u} ofReal(r(b)^k) ≤ ofReal(10^k·M).

audit.reason: The packing quantifier, countability requirement and ENNReal sum match the prose exactly. Bounded-radius closed-ball Vitali covering with factor 5, ball_volume at radius 5r, and outer-measure subadditivity prove the conclusion. Neither measurability of S nor M ≥ 0 is missing. The proof uses only its declared sibling dependency. For the selected parent, measurable positive disjoint tubes establish the packing condition for every disjoint subfamily; cancellation of positive finite μ(univ) gives M = 1/β. Together with the zero-mass case, this yields exactly dgc_periodic_maximal.
